docs.text: Anyone who lives near the Great Lakes, since it's mostly fresh water can I just drink straight out of it? Or is it too cold to drink?
Right? I keep wondering when the fresh water conversation is going to start. The Midwest/Great Lakes region is the best kept secret in the U.S. I hope it’s never discovered.
Yeah, this is likely the case. Definitely I would never drink water near a large city on the Great Lakes straight out of the lake, ever

Wow I never thought NYC would have this problem. Here, if I walk into a dive bar that at first glance doesn't have anything drinkable, I know I can always get a decent drink just by asking "what do you have that's great lakes?" They always have something. Everyone does.
I have been drinking La Fin du Monde for decades, and only today actually recognized the St. Lawerence River and the Great Lakes way down in the bottom left of the label.

I grew up going camping a lot. I would not drink out of the great lakes unless I had a specialized filtration pump. I say this as a the kid who drank boiled water from lakes we camped by and who would get so very sick (the runs) every time anyway.

Back in 2017 I joined the Great Lakes Water Walk with hundreds of other folks, choosing the western leg which began at sunrise on the mouth of the Credit River. We crossed here around 9:30… I burst into tears. This is the water I know best, where I visit most often and clean the banks. I 🩵 it here.

also my reading comprehension is apparently terrible this morning because the OP mentioned being sluggish from the cold! The ionic imbalance from freshwater would fuck him up too. Maybe he could use some gatorade to fuel his Great Lakes adventure?

Lmfao that's not true. Just any of the lakes besides the couple of north ones in the U.S, or in western Canada are gross. But the great lakes are mostly okay. Only lake Ontario is truly nasty. :p don't go there. But you don't have to worry bout that. Any natural spring is nice, just don't drink it.
Makes me glad my folks moved us to the Great Lakes area and I can have drinkable water.
You can have Great Lakes water when you pry it from my cold, dead hands. I am not kidding. Come and take it.

The temperature isn’t the problem for drinking There are tons of chemicals and contaminants and bacteria and fungi in the Great Lakes. I used to live right next to Lake Superior. You would need a solid filtration system. Or go find the mouth of a natural spring to drink out of

This is why when my wife and I decided where we wanted to plant our family after getting out of the service, we picked a Great Lakes state right as close to our Great Lake as we could. If freshwater is going to be so important, living right next to the largest source of it anywhere is a hedge.
It's good, we need it. We need to replenish the Great Lakes and ground water after last falls dry spell.
Great Lakes Water. Keep that front of mind.
I live less than a mile from Lake Michigan, part of the largest freshwater system in the world, and it blows my mind at how much stuff continues to be built in brittle arid ecosystems
We Drink From Our Own Wells (Lake Michigan)
Fresh water is the best water. Lake Superior, 2024
